basic_identification.name: On-chain art / fully on-chain SVG
basic_identification.originator: Larva Labs (Matt Hall, John Watkinson) -- Autoglyphs (2019), first fully on-chain art. Mathcastles (0x113d, xaltgeist) -- Terraforms (2021), fully on-chain SVG/animation. Art Blocks (Erick Calderon) moved progressively to on-chain storage. Other key projects: Loot (Dom Hofmann), Nouns (on-chain generative avatars), Strange Attractors.
basic_identification.geography: Global, internet-native. No geographic center. Autoglyphs and CryptoPunks from Larva Labs (Canada/US). Mathcastles anonymous. Art Blocks US-based. The practice is inherently borderless -- the blockchain is the territory.

core_ideas.core_claim: Art stored entirely on blockchain has no external dependencies. The code that generates the art, the metadata, and the visual representation all live on-chain, ensuring permanence, immutability, and self-sufficiency as long as the blockchain exists. This is the most radical position on digital art preservation: the art is the algorithm, and the algorithm is on-chain forever.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Maximally digitally native. The blockchain itself is the medium -- not a distribution mechanism but the material substrate. On-chain constraints (gas costs, block size limits, Solidity language) shape the aesthetic. SVG and ASCII art dominate because they are compact text formats storable as strings in smart contracts. The constraint of on-chain storage produces a distinctive aesthetic of elegant compression. Terraforms' 32x32 grid of animated text characters is specifically shaped by EVM limitations.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Resistant by architecture. On-chain art does not depend on platform visibility, social media, or marketplace attention for its existence. The art persists on-chain regardless of whether anyone looks at it. However, the market value and cultural recognition of on-chain art do depend on community attention and collector interest. The purity of on-chain storage is an infrastructure principle, not an attention-economy strategy.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Strongly intention-native. On-chain art addresses the most fundamental structural need in digital art: permanence and independence from intermediaries. It is infrastructure-level intention, solving the problem that digital art depends on servers, platforms, and companies that may disappear. The Autoglyphs ethos -- the art and its creation mechanism preserved indefinitely on the blockchain -- is a pure expression of intention over attention.

market_economics.revenue_model: Primary mint sales (buyers pay gas + mint price). Secondary market trading on OpenSea and other marketplaces. Creator royalties (enforcement varies). No subscription or institutional revenue. The art is its own economic infrastructure -- the smart contract handles sales, royalties, and ownership transfers.
market_economics.market_position: Primary market (minting) and secondary market (trading). Autoglyphs are positioned as blue-chip digital art collectibles, comparable to CryptoPunks in cultural significance. Terraforms occupy a niche collector market. Art Blocks' fully on-chain projects span the market from emerging to established.
market_economics.price_range: Autoglyphs: $100K-$1M+ per piece (10 sold for ~$14.5M in Feb 2024, Sotheby's estimated set of seven at $3.5M+ in Oct 2024). Terraforms: 0.2-1 ETH floor (~$500-$2,500). Other on-chain projects: wide range from sub-$100 to five figures. The on-chain premium commands higher prices for projects perceived as culturally significant.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Stable for blue-chip projects (Autoglyphs hold value). Terraforms community active but volume modest. Art Blocks' move to 90% fully on-chain by 2024 normalizes on-chain storage. New on-chain experiments continue (Bitcoin Ordinals/inscriptions expand the practice to Bitcoin). L2 scaling reduces gas costs, enabling more on-chain experimentation. Volume is lower than 2021-2022 peaks but the practice is structurally healthy.
market_economics.collector_demographics: Hardcore crypto-native collectors who understand and value on-chain permanence. Technical sophisticates who can verify on-chain storage. Institutional collectors (Centre Pompidou, Whitney Museum have acquired Autoglyphs). A small but dedicated collector base that prioritizes provenance and permanence over visual spectacle. [uncertain]
market_economics.sustainability: Strong for the practice. On-chain art has zero ongoing hosting costs -- the art exists on the blockchain without maintenance. The practice does not depend on any company or platform surviving. Market sustainability depends on continued collector interest, but the art's permanence means it outlasts market cycles. The most sustainable model in digital art by structural design.

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Solidity (Ethereum smart contract language), SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics as text strings), ASCII/Unicode text, JavaScript for rendering (when needed), custom fonts. EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine) as the execution environment. Hardware: Ethereum network nodes. Development: Remix IDE, Hardhat, Foundry. The constraint of on-chain storage drives creative use of compact formats.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: Largely irrelevant. On-chain art is algorithmic (human-authored code) not AI-based. The constraint of on-chain storage (compact code) is antithetical to large AI models. Some intersection with on-chain generative systems that could theoretically incorporate lightweight ML, but the practice is defined by algorithmic elegance and code compression, not by AI capability.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Diverse. Autoglyphs: static ASCII art rendered from on-chain data. Terraforms: animated SVG that cycles colors and characters in real-time in the browser. Terraforms also support interactivity (Daydream and Terraform modes for drawing and recording on-chain). Some on-chain projects are fully static; others are dynamic runtime art.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Distinctive and well-defined. Key terms: fully on-chain, on-chain art, runtime art, EVM art, code-as-art, gas-limited aesthetics, on-chain permanence, algorithmic compression, cave paintings of on-chain art (Autoglyphs nickname). Terraforms added: hypercastle, terraforming, daydream mode. The vocabulary reflects the technical constraints and philosophical commitments of the practice. The aesthetic is defined by elegant minimalism within extreme constraints.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Strongly infrastructure over spectacle (permanence is the point, not visual impact). Openness (on-chain code is inspectable and verifiable). Individual authorship but commons-contributing (open source of many projects, inspectable code that enables learning). The practice is the most infrastructure-committed position in digital art.

infrastructure_governance.openness: High. On-chain code is inherently inspectable -- anyone can read the smart contract. Autoglyphs' algorithm is fully visible. Terraforms' code is on-chain and readable. Many projects are effectively open-source by architecture (the code is public on the blockchain even if not formally licensed).
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Smart contract governance. Once deployed, the code is immutable and self-executing. No curatorial committee, no platform governance, no corporate control. Nouns DAO extends this to community governance of the project's treasury and direction. Terraforms' community has self-organized tools and visualizers. Governance is minimized by design -- the code is the governance.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Maximum sovereignty. The art, metadata, and rendering logic are all on-chain. No external server, no platform dependency, no corporate gatekeeper. Ownership is cryptographically verified. The owner controls their token completely. If every platform and marketplace disappears, the art still exists and can be rendered by anyone with an Ethereum node.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Excellent for Ethereum ecosystem. ERC-721 standard tokens. Compatible with all Ethereum marketplaces and wallets. SVG output can be rendered by any browser. The art is maximally portable within its ecosystem. Cross-chain interoperability is limited (Ethereum-specific). Ordinals bring similar principles to Bitcoin.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: The strongest preservation model in digital art. On-chain storage means the art persists as long as the blockchain exists. No server maintenance, no hosting costs, no renewal required. The code is immutable and redundantly stored across thousands of nodes worldwide. Rendering depends on browser SVG/JavaScript support, which is a dependency but a very robust one. Autoglyphs are now in the Centre Pompidou and Whitney Museum permanent collections, adding institutional preservation.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Binary: creators deploy contracts, collectors mint tokens. Smart contract terms are take-it-or-leave-it. Terraforms' mode changes (Terrain to Daydream) are permanent and require holder consent (transaction signing). No granular consent beyond the smart contract's built-in mechanics.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Growing institutional recognition. Centre Pompidou and Whitney Museum have acquired Autoglyphs. Sotheby's has held dedicated Autoglyphs auctions. The practice is gaining art-historical legitimacy as a foundational moment in digital art. However, the technical barrier to understanding on-chain art limits broader art-world engagement.
field_position.what_it_enables: True digital art permanence without institutional dependency. Art that is self-contained and self-authenticating. A new medium (code-within-EVM-constraints) that produces distinctive aesthetics. Verifiable provenance and ownership without trusted intermediaries. Community-built tools and extensions (Terraforms ecosystem).
field_position.what_it_lacks: Accessibility for non-technical audiences. Visual richness (on-chain constraints limit complexity). Connection to broader art discourse beyond the crypto-art community. Preservation of the full experience (rendering environment may change). Standards for what counts as truly on-chain (many projects claim on-chain status with varying degrees of accuracy).
field_position.who_is_excluded: Non-technical collectors (understanding on-chain vs. off-chain requires blockchain literacy). Artists without Solidity/smart contract skills. Those who cannot afford Ethereum gas fees. Anyone without a crypto wallet. The practice's extreme technicality creates the highest barrier to entry in digital art. Visual art practitioners without coding skills are entirely excluded from creation.
field_position.frontier_signal: Established principle, evolving implementations. The concept of fully on-chain art is now established (since 2019). The frontier has moved to: on-chain art on Bitcoin (Ordinals), L2 experimentation (cheaper on-chain storage), more complex on-chain rendering (Terraforms pushed boundaries), and community-governed on-chain worlds.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Crypto-art community (Twitter/X), marketplace listings (OpenSea), auction house events (Sotheby's), specialized media (Right Click Save, Le Random), community forums. On-chain explorers (Etherscan) enable direct discovery of contracts. The FullyOnChain.art directory provides a curated catalog.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: Very low at the infrastructure level -- the art exists regardless of attention. Moderate at the market level -- secondary market prices depend on collector interest. The practice's permanence principle means it is designed to outlast attention cycles. Blue-chip on-chain projects (Autoglyphs) have maintained value through the crash, suggesting attention-resilience.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Maximally intention-native. The practice addresses the most fundamental structural need in digital art: permanence and self-sufficiency. Every design decision serves this intention. No engagement optimization, no attention capture. The art exists to exist, not to be seen.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Significant. On-chain code is inherently public and inspectable. The practice establishes permanence standards that benefit the broader field. Concepts like runtime art, EVM art, and gas-limited aesthetics contribute to shared vocabulary. The practice demonstrates that digital art does not need to depend on platforms or institutions for survival.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Both ownership and creation. On-chain provenance includes: who deployed the contract, when, the exact code, every mint event, every transfer. This is the most complete ownership provenance in digital art. However, meaning provenance (critical reception, exhibition history, cultural significance) is not on-chain.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Archival with permanence emphasis. On-chain records are immutable and permanent. Block timestamps provide exact temporal anchoring. Terraforms' animation introduces real-time temporality within the archival frame. The practice's fundamental temporal commitment is to eternity -- art that persists as long as the blockchain.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: The practice implicitly addresses the absence of permanence in digital art -- it exists as a solution to the problem of digital art's ephemerality. Autoglyphs' nickname ('cave paintings of on-chain art') positions them as the first marks in a new permanent medium, defined against the absence of prior on-chain art.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Coherence around a principle (on-chain permanence) with diverse aesthetic implementations. Autoglyphs' minimalist ASCII, Terraforms' animated text grids, Nouns' pixel art, and various SVG projects represent different aesthetic approaches united by the shared commitment to on-chain storage.
coherence.contestability: Moderate. The definition of fully on-chain is actively contested: does the rendering layer count? What about JavaScript dependencies? Is it truly on-chain if it needs a browser to view? These are productive debates. Smart contract terms are immutable once deployed, so individual project rules are not contestable.
coherence.forkability: High. On-chain code is public and inspectable. Anyone can deploy similar contracts. However, the cultural significance and network effects of first-mover projects (Autoglyphs) cannot be forked. The technical approach is fully forkable; the cultural meaning is not.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The permanence principle: infrastructure should outlast any single platform or institution. The self-sufficiency model: no external dependencies for core functionality. The inspectable-by-design approach: all A(DAI) intelligence should be verifiable and auditable. The constraint-driven aesthetic: working within limitations produces distinctive quality. The community tool-building ecosystem (Terraforms' Hypercastle Explorer) as a model for commons participation.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The extreme technicality that excludes non-developers. The ownership-only provenance model (A(DAI) needs meaning provenance). The visual minimalism imposed by storage constraints (A(DAI) must accommodate all media). The Ethereum-only dependency. The binary smart-contract governance (A(DAI) needs nuanced, contestable governance).
adai_comparison.structural_tension: On-chain art represents the most uncompromising position on digital permanence. A(DAI) aspires to permanence but cannot accept the trade-offs: on-chain storage limits media richness, excludes non-technical participants, and locks governance into immutable code. A(DAI) must find a middle path between on-chain art's radical self-sufficiency and traditional digital art's fragile platform-dependency. The question: can A(DAI) achieve durable permanence without requiring everything to live on a single blockchain?

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Crypto/NFT regulations apply to token sales and trading. No specific regulation of on-chain art as distinct from other NFTs. Copyright law applies to the code and generated outputs. The immutability of on-chain art creates regulatory challenges: content cannot be removed even if ordered. Smart contract functionality may face increasing regulatory scrutiny.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Code copyright belongs to the deploying artist. The on-chain code is public (visible to all) but copyright still applies. License terms vary by project. Nouns uses CC0 (public domain). Most projects do not explicitly license their on-chain code. The immutability of on-chain storage means IP enforcement is practically impossible -- the code cannot be removed from the blockchain.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in. Artists choose to deploy on-chain. Collectors choose to mint. Terraforms' mode changes require active holder consent. No opt-out possible for already-deployed code (immutability). The permanence principle means there is no undo.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Ethereum blockchain (primary). Bitcoin blockchain (Ordinals/inscriptions). No platform dependency beyond the blockchain itself -- this is the entire point. Rendering depends on web browsers (SVG, JavaScript). Marketplace dependency for trading but not for existence. The lowest platform dependency of any digital art practice.
ecosystem.network_effects: Moderate. The practice benefits from Ethereum's network effects (large node network, broad wallet adoption, marketplace infrastructure). Cultural network effects around blue-chip projects (Autoglyphs' status attracts collectors and imitators). Community network effects (Terraforms' active community builds tools and extensions).
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Resilient. Autoglyphs maintained high value through the crash (institutional collecting, Sotheby's auctions in 2024). Terraforms community remains active. Art Blocks' move to 90% on-chain shows industry adoption of the principle. Bitcoin Ordinals expanded the practice to a new blockchain. The practice's permanence commitment makes it structurally resistant to market cycles -- the art persists regardless of price.
